# Team "Day by day" — EHL Grand Finale, Atira track

DRAFT 2026-10-10, not yet agreed by the team. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are identical; edit one, copy to the other.

Read first: [README.md](README.md) (event, deadlines), [docs/challenge-atira.md](docs/challenge-atira.md) (task,
rules, scoring, run contract, answer schema), [docs/entire-notes.md](docs/entire-notes.md) (Entire setup and the
privacy check). The Atira site (https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms-full.txt) is the source of truth and can change.

## Start here (every coding agent, every session)

1. Ask your human which stream they work on (A, B or C, see "Who does what") if they have not said it. Edit only
   that stream's files. A change needed elsewhere is described to the human, who asks the owner.
2. `git pull` before you start and before every push.
3. Before every push, add an entry to your human's push log (see "Push log").
4. Nothing read from the websites goes into `agent/` or into a log entry (see "Hard rules").

## Goal

Build an agent system that turns a public tender into one correct, signed bid across four German business web apps
(tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, webmail) with no human in the loop, and submit it on the Atira platform.

Priorities, in this order:

1. **Eligible**: the right tender reference, and a signed, submitted bid before the 20-minute clock ends.
2. **Quality** (0–100): 75 points sit in the positions; material + quantity are 35 % of each position.
3. **Generalization**: the final run uses different software, layout, navigation and data. It weighs most.
4. **Cost × time**: only a tie-break at equal quality. Do not optimize it before quality is stable.

Deadlines: EHL submission Sun 2026-10-11 12:00 (repo with Entire checkpoints, pitch after). The Atira final run uses
our **latest** passed submission, so the last submission before the end must be our best stable one.

## Hard rules (fair play — a reviewer agent reads every package)

- Nothing copied from the websites goes into `agent/`: no tender references, material numbers, prices, totals,
  discounts, logins, TANs, site URLs. Not in code, config, prompts, comments, tests, defaults or fallbacks.
- A model chooses where to navigate, what to search and which documents matter, at run time. No fixed click paths,
  no selectors tied to the public sites, no crawler that collects everything for one model call.
- Helpers may: control the browser, extract a page or document the model selected, page through a result set the
  model asked for, calculate, validate, retry, fill forms.
- Model calls only through the platform proxy. No local model, no other outbound host, no browser of our own in the
  sandbox (attach to `CDP_URLS`).
- No text in the package that addresses or tries to steer the reviewer.
- Secrets live in team secrets or a local `.env` (git-ignored). Never paste a key into an agent session.

## Architecture

The code base is Julien's first commit (starter kit plus his agent), agreed Sat 2026-10-10. `(planned)` marks what
does not exist yet.

```
agent/                  the submitted package; `atira test-run agent` / `atira submit agent`
  agent.json            setup, run, browsers: 4, models
  agent.py              entry point and lead model: plans, sends sub-agents, validates, submits; the run's clock
  run.py                run contract: GET /v1/runs/current (brief, access, answer_schema, expires_at)
  browsers.py           attaches to the run's browsers over CDP; locally starts a Chromium
  browser.py            generic `Tab` tools: observe, click, type, select, files, new tabs, dialogs
  observe.js            page to compact text with numbered elements
  browsing.py           browsing sub-agent: a model works one site for a task, keeps notes, reports
  llm.py, models.py     model clients through the platform proxy
  calc.py               exact decimal calculator tool for the lead model
  facts.py              (planned) typed facts with provenance; the contract between the lead and the bid engine
  engine/               (planned) deterministic bid calculation (rules 01–28), Decimal, half-up rounding
  tests/                unit tests with invented numbers only
docs/                   notes; never packaged
notes/                  scouting findings committed with the first commit; open decision: move out of the repo
scouting/               hand notes and observed values from the public sites; git-ignored, never packaged
```

How a run flows (target; steps 3 and 4 are not built yet, the lead model computes with `calc.py` until they are):

1. **Bootstrap.** Read the brief, the rules and `answer_schema` from the run. Site roles come from the brief and
   `access`, not from hard-coded names.
2. **Lead model + four site sub-agents** (one browser each, in parallel). The lead hands sub-agents tasks that
   depend on other sites' answers: final quantity → ERP price scale; Kataloggruppe from the specification → ERP
   search; Q&A keys → the matching rule mail; tender reference → mail search.
3. **Facts with provenance.** Every fact records the site, document, date, sender and revision it came from, so the
   authority and time rules (latest record not after the scenario date, exact reference, authorized sender) are
   applied in code, not left to the model's memory.
4. **Bid engine.** Pure functions from facts to the answer object. No model in the arithmetic. Unrounded components,
   one half-up rounding at the end, breakdown fields reported separately.
5. **Validate and submit.** Check against the run's schema and our own arithmetic consistency, then a sub-agent
   fills the configurator, fetches the TAN from the webmail, signs, and confirms the receipt.
6. **Deadline guard.** At a fixed margin before `expires_at`, submit what is complete and omit unfinished positions
   explicitly. A run without an answer scores 0.

Choices made for now: Python 3.12 with uv and Playwright over CDP (the starter kit's stack); Qwen as the default
model because it is cheap in the cost ranking; a frontier model through the proxy only where a test run shows it
buys quality.

Build order: baseline test run of the current agent → reference + decision + material + quantity end to end with a
signed bid → base price, discount, lead time → advanced pricing layers (clauses, FX, packaging, setup pools, bonus,
metal indices) → cost × time.

## Who does what (proposal, Sat 2026-10-10)

Three streams, split by files so that nobody edits another stream's files. Each person's coding agent works only
inside that person's stream.

| Who | Stream | Files only this stream edits | Work |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Julien** | A: sites and reading | `browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`, `browsers.py`, `tests/test_browser*` | Sub-agent reports that are complete and exact on each site: documents, paging, revisions, session timeouts, look-alike records; nothing tied to the public sites' layout; pitch and development story |
| **Uzunov** | B: bid engine | `facts.py`, `engine/`, `tests/test_engine*` | Rule walkthrough 01–28; typed facts; deterministic calculation in layers (core first, then advanced pricing); cases with invented numbers |
| **Orhun** (captain) | C: lead, submission, runs | `agent.py`, `llm.py`, `models.py`, `run.py`, `calc.py`, `agent.json`, repo files (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/` except the others' push logs) | Lead prompts and flow; reports to typed facts; submission (configurator, TAN, signature, receipt); deadline guard; test runs and score breakdowns; Entire and repo hygiene; every `atira submit` |

How the streams meet:

- `facts.py` is the only shared contract. Stream B owns it; a change is announced in the commit message and the
  other streams adapt.
- Stream A's interface is the sub-agent report (`BrowsingAgent.run()`); stream B's is one function from facts to
  the answer object. Stream C calls both and changes neither.
- A change needed in another stream's file is requested from its owner, not made.
- Local runs with the scouting logins are free for everyone. Sandbox test runs go through stream C (the team limit
  is two running, three waiting); A and B ask for one when they need a score.
- Small commits, pull before every push.

Shared rules for all coding agents:

- Never run `atira submit`, `atira cancel` on a scored run, or `atira final` without Orhun's explicit yes.
- Write what a test run taught us into `docs/` (how the sites behave, not their values), so the other streams and
  the pitch can use it.
- Talk to Orhun in Turkish; write files, code and commit messages in English.

## Push log

Every push adds one entry to the pusher's own file, so the others (people and agents) can see what changed without
reading the diff. One file per person, so entries never conflict:
`docs/log/julien.md`, `docs/log/uzunov.md`, `docs/log/orhun.md`. Newest entry on top.

```markdown
## 2026-10-10 14:30 · short title

- Changed: which files, and what they do now
- Why: the problem or the score field this is for
- Checked: unit tests, local run or test run id, and the result
- Learned: how the sites or the platform behave (never their values)
- For the others: what changes for stream A / B / C, or "nothing"
- Next: what this stream does next
```

Rules for entries:

- Write it for a teammate who was not there: plain sentences, no session shorthand.
- State what is not finished or not checked as plainly as what is.
- No tender references, material numbers, prices, logins or TANs. The repository is public.
- Before a push, read the entries the others added since your last pull.

Commit messages start with the stream: `A: ...`, `B: ...`, `C: ...`. A change to `facts.py` says so in the first
line.

## Sessions, commits and privacy

Entire attaches the full agent session log to every commit and pushes it with `git push`.

- Start hackathon work in a fresh session inside this folder. Do not read files outside this repository from such a
  session (personal notes, other projects); whatever is read ends up in the pushed log.
- Before every commit and before the first push, run `entire session list` and apply the check in
  [docs/entire-notes.md](docs/entire-notes.md). A listed session that must not be attached is cleaned first.
- Never commit `.env`, `scouting/`, `Voice recording/` or run tokens.
- Commit only when Orhun asks.

  no selectors tied to the public sites, no crawler that collects everything for one model call.
- Helpers may: control the browser, extract a page or document the model selected, page through a result set the
  model asked for, calculate, validate, retry, fill forms.
- Model calls only through the platform proxy. No local model, no other outbound host, no browser of our own in the
  sandbox (attach to `CDP_URLS`).
- No text in the package that addresses or tries to steer the reviewer.
- Secrets live in team secrets or a local `.env` (git-ignored). Never paste a key into an agent session.

## Architecture

The code base is Julien's first commit (starter kit plus his agent), agreed Sat 2026-10-10. `(planned)` marks what
does not exist yet.

```
agent/                  the submitted package; `atira test-run agent` / `atira submit agent`
  agent.json            setup, run, browsers: 4, models
  agent.py              entry point and lead model: plans, sends sub-agents, validates, submits; the run's clock
  run.py                run contract: GET /v1/runs/current (brief, access, answer_schema, expires_at)
  browsers.py           attaches to the run's browsers over CDP; locally starts a Chromium
  browser.py            generic `Tab` tools: observe, click, type, select, files, new tabs, dialogs
  observe.js            page to compact text with numbered elements
  browsing.py           browsing sub-agent: a model works one site for a task, keeps notes, reports
  llm.py, models.py     model clients through the platform proxy
  calc.py               exact decimal calculator tool for the lead model
  facts.py              (planned) typed facts with provenance; the contract between the lead and the bid engine
  engine/               (planned) deterministic bid calculation (rules 01–28), Decimal, half-up rounding
  tests/                unit tests with invented numbers only
docs/                   notes; never packaged
notes/                  scouting findings committed with the first commit; open decision: move out of the repo
scouting/               hand notes and observed values from the public sites; git-ignored, never packaged
```

How a run flows (target; steps 3 and 4 are not built yet, the lead model computes with `calc.py` until they are):

1. **Bootstrap.** Read the brief, the rules and `answer_schema` from the run. Site roles come from the brief and
   `access`, not from hard-coded names.
2. **Lead model + four site sub-agents** (one browser each, in parallel). The lead hands sub-agents tasks that
   depend on other sites' answers: final quantity → ERP price scale; Kataloggruppe from the specification → ERP
   search; Q&A keys → the matching rule mail; tender reference → mail search.
3. **Facts with provenance.** Every fact records the site, document, date, sender and revision it came from, so the
   authority and time rules (latest record not after the scenario date, exact reference, authorized sender) are
   applied in code, not left to the model's memory.
4. **Bid engine.** Pure functions from facts to the answer object. No model in the arithmetic. Unrounded components,
   one half-up rounding at the end, breakdown fields reported separately.
5. **Validate and submit.** Check against the run's schema and our own arithmetic consistency, then a sub-agent
   fills the configurator, fetches the TAN from the webmail, signs, and confirms the receipt.
6. **Deadline guard.** At a fixed margin before `expires_at`, submit what is complete and omit unfinished positions
   explicitly. A run without an answer scores 0.

Choices made for now: Python 3.12 with uv and Playwright over CDP (the starter kit's stack); Qwen as the default
model because it is cheap in the cost ranking; a frontier model through the proxy only where a test run shows it
buys quality.

Build order: baseline test run of the current agent → reference + decision + material + quantity end to end with a
signed bid → base price, discount, lead time → advanced pricing layers (clauses, FX, packaging, setup pools, bonus,
metal indices) → cost × time.

## Who does what (proposal, Sat 2026-10-10)

Three streams, split by files so that nobody edits another stream's files. Each person's coding agent works only
inside that person's stream.

| **Julien** | A: sites and reading | `browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`, `browsers.py`, `tests/test_browser*` | Sub-agent reports that are complete and exact on each site: documents, paging, revisions, session timeouts, look-alike records; nothing tied to the public sites' layout; pitch and development story |
| **Uzunov** | B: bid engine | `facts.py`, `engine/`, `tests/test_engine*` | Rule walkthrough 01–28; typed facts; deterministic calculation in layers (core first, then advanced pricing); cases with invented numbers |

How the streams meet:

- `facts.py` is the only shared contract. Stream B owns it; a change is announced in the commit message and the
  other streams adapt.
- Stream A's interface is the sub-agent report (`BrowsingAgent.run()`); stream B's is one function from facts to

- Never run `atira submit`, `atira cancel` on a scored run, or `atira final` without Orhun's explicit yes.
- Write what a test run taught us into `docs/` (how the sites behave, not their values), so the other streams and
  the pitch can use it.

## Push log

Every push adds one entry to the pusher's own file, so the others (people and agents) can see what changed without
reading the diff. One file per person, so entries never conflict:
`docs/log/julien.md`, `docs/log/uzunov.md`, `docs/log/orhun.md`. Newest entry on top.

```markdown
## 2026-10-10 14:30 · short title

- Changed: which files, and what they do now
- Why: the problem or the score field this is for
- Checked: unit tests, local run or test run id, and the result
- Learned: how the sites or the platform behave (never their values)
- For the others: what changes for stream A / B / C, or "nothing"
- Next: what this stream does next
```

Rules for entries:

- Write it for a teammate who was not there: plain sentences, no session shorthand.
- State what is not finished or not checked as plainly as what is.
- No tender references, material numbers, prices, logins or TANs. The repository is public.
- Before a push, read the entries the others added since your last pull.

Commit messages start with the stream: `A: ...`, `B: ...`, `C: ...`. A change to `facts.py` says so in the first
line.

## Sessions, commits and privacy

Entire attaches the full agent session log to every commit and pushes it with `git push`.

- Start hackathon work in a fresh session inside this folder. Do not read files outside this repository from such a

+# Work streams — who builds what, and where the streams meet
+Written Sat 2026-10-10 for the three people on the team and for their coding agents. The short table is in
+[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), section "Who does what"; this file is the detail. If you are a coding agent, read
+"How the agent works today", then the section of your human's stream, then "Where the streams meet".
+The work is split by files. Each file has exactly one stream that may edit it. That is what lets three people and
+their agents work at the same time without merge conflicts and without undoing each other's decisions.
+Everything submitted to Atira is the folder `agent/`. One run goes like this:
+1. `agent.py` reads the run (`run.py`: the brief with the bid rules, each website's address and login, the answer
+   schema, the expiry time) and opens one browser tab per website (`browsers.py`, `browser.py`).
+2. A **lead model** (`Orchestrator` in `agent.py`) reads the brief. It cannot browse. It has three tools:
+   - `investigate(site, task)` sends a **browsing sub-agent** (`BrowsingAgent` in `browsing.py`) to one website with
+     a task in plain language. The sub-agent drives the browser through a text view of the page (`observe.js`,
+     `Tab` in `browser.py`), takes notes, and returns one text report. Several sites run in parallel.
+   - `submit_bid(answer, hints)` checks the answer against the schema, then sends a sub-agent to type the bid into
+     the tender website's form, fetch the signing code from the mailbox, sign and confirm.
+3. The lead model decides what to ask next from the reports, works out the bid, and submits.
+What is weak in this design, and why the streams exist:
+- The reports are free text. A value that was read wrongly, or from the wrong record, is not caught anywhere.
+- The lead model applies about 28 bid rules by itself, one calculator call at a time. Money is scored to the cent,
+  and 75 of 100 points sit in the positions.
+- The final run uses different websites. Anything that only works because of how the public websites look fails
+**Goal.** A sub-agent that is sent to any of the websites with a task comes back with a report that is complete,
+exact (values as shown, with units and dates) and says where each value was read. This must hold on software the
+**What the other streams rely on (do not change without telling stream C first).**
+- `Tab(site_id, page)` and `BrowsingAgent(model, tabs, credentials, task, context, name=..., deadline=...,
+  max_steps=..., log=...)`, as `agent.py` calls them today.
+- `await BrowsingAgent.run()` returns one string: the report, then the notes taken while browsing.
+1. Run one sub-agent per website on your machine with a survey task and compare its report with what you see in
+   the browser yourself. Every difference is a bug in this stream.
+2. Documents: PDF and ZIP files, documents inside embedded frames and nested viewers. Known gap: `browser.py`
+   imports `pypdf` to read PDFs, but `pypdf` is not in `agent/pyproject.toml`, so in the sandbox every PDF comes
+   back as "could not be read". Ask stream C to add the dependency.
+3. Lists: paging, "load more", searches that must be narrowed before they show results.
+4. Versions: a site that opens an old revision first; the report must say which revision a value comes from and
+   which one the site marks as current.
+5. Sessions and errors: a session that expires and returns to the sign-in page, error pages that work on a retry,
+6. Look-alike records: the report must name the exact reference, sender and date of what it read, so a record for
+   another tender is recognisable as such.
+7. Generalisation check: no selector, text, URL or page order that only exists on the public websites. The sign-in
+   helper in `browsing.py` finds fields by their type, which is fine; keep it that way.
+8. Only when the reports are reliable: fewer steps and tokens per report.
+**Done when** a report contains every value the task asked for, as shown on the site, each with its source (page
+or document, date, sender, revision), and says plainly what it could not find.
+**Not this stream.** Bid rules, arithmetic, the lead model's prompts, the submission flow. Also the pitch and the
+development story belong to Julien, outside the code.
+**Goal.** One function that turns collected facts into the answer object, correct to the cent, with no model
+involved. The same facts always give the same bid.
+- `facts.py`: typed records (dataclasses) for everything the rules need. Every fact carries where it came from:
+  website, document or record, date, sender, revision. This file is the contract between the streams; a change is
+  announced in the first line of the commit message.
+- One entry point, proposed as `engine.build_bid(facts) -> dict`, returning an object that matches the answer
+- `Decimal` only, never `float`. Components stay unrounded; round half-up once at the end (rule 27).

# Work streams — who builds what, and where the streams meet

Written Sat 2026-10-10 for the three people on the team and for their coding agents. The short table is in
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), section "Who does what"; this file is the detail. If you are a coding agent, read
"How the agent works today", then the section of your human's stream, then "Where the streams meet".

The work is split by files. Each file has exactly one stream that may edit it. That is what lets three people and
their agents work at the same time without merge conflicts and without undoing each other's decisions.

## How the agent works today

Everything submitted to Atira is the folder `agent/`. One run goes like this:

1. `agent.py` reads the run (`run.py`: the brief with the bid rules, each website's address and login, the answer
   schema, the expiry time) and opens one browser tab per website (`browsers.py`, `browser.py`).
2. A **lead model** (`Orchestrator` in `agent.py`) reads the brief. It cannot browse. It has three tools:
   - `investigate(site, task)` sends a **browsing sub-agent** (`BrowsingAgent` in `browsing.py`) to one website with
     a task in plain language. The sub-agent drives the browser through a text view of the page (`observe.js`,
     `Tab` in `browser.py`), takes notes, and returns one text report. Several sites run in parallel.
   - `calculate(expression)` does exact decimal arithmetic (`calc.py`).
   - `submit_bid(answer, hints)` checks the answer against the schema, then sends a sub-agent to type the bid into
     the tender website's form, fetch the signing code from the mailbox, sign and confirm.
3. The lead model decides what to ask next from the reports, works out the bid, and submits.

What is weak in this design, and why the streams exist:

- The reports are free text. A value that was read wrongly, or from the wrong record, is not caught anywhere.
- The lead model applies about 28 bid rules by itself, one calculator call at a time. Money is scored to the cent,
  and 75 of 100 points sit in the positions.
- The final run uses different websites. Anything that only works because of how the public websites look fails
  there.

## Stream A — sites and reading (Julien)

**Goal.** A sub-agent that is sent to any of the websites with a task comes back with a report that is complete,
exact (values as shown, with units and dates) and says where each value was read. This must hold on software the
agent has never seen.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/browser.py`, `agent/observe.js`, `agent/browsing.py`,
`agent/browsers.py`, `agent/tests/test_browser*.py`, `docs/log/julien.md`.

**What the other streams rely on (do not change without telling stream C first).**
- `Tab(site_id, page)` and `BrowsingAgent(model, tabs, credentials, task, context, name=..., deadline=...,
  max_steps=..., log=...)`, as `agent.py` calls them today.
- `await BrowsingAgent.run()` returns one string: the report, then the notes taken while browsing.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Run one sub-agent per website on your machine with a survey task and compare its report with what you see in
   the browser yourself. Every difference is a bug in this stream.
2. Documents: PDF and ZIP files, documents inside embedded frames and nested viewers. Known gap: `browser.py`
   imports `pypdf` to read PDFs, but `pypdf` is not in `agent/pyproject.toml`, so in the sandbox every PDF comes
   back as "could not be read". Ask stream C to add the dependency.
3. Lists: paging, "load more", searches that must be narrowed before they show results.
4. Versions: a site that opens an old revision first; the report must say which revision a value comes from and
   which one the site marks as current.
5. Sessions and errors: a session that expires and returns to the sign-in page, error pages that work on a retry,
   popups and dialogs.
6. Look-alike records: the report must name the exact reference, sender and date of what it read, so a record for
   another tender is recognisable as such.
7. Generalisation check: no selector, text, URL or page order that only exists on the public websites. The sign-in
   helper in `browsing.py` finds fields by their type, which is fine; keep it that way.
8. Only when the reports are reliable: fewer steps and tokens per report.

**Done when** a report contains every value the task asked for, as shown on the site, each with its source (page
or document, date, sender, revision), and says plainly what it could not find.

**Not this stream.** Bid rules, arithmetic, the lead model's prompts, the submission flow. Also the pitch and the
development story belong to Julien, outside the code.

## Stream B — bid engine (Uzunov)

**Goal.** One function that turns collected facts into the answer object, correct to the cent, with no model
involved. The same facts always give the same bid.

**Files only this stream edits (all new).** `agent/facts.py`, `agent/engine/`, `agent/tests/test_engine*.py`,
`docs/log/uzunov.md`.

**What the other streams rely on.**
- `facts.py`: typed records (dataclasses) for everything the rules need. Every fact carries where it came from:
  website, document or record, date, sender, revision. This file is the contract between the streams; a change is
  announced in the first line of the commit message.
- One entry point, proposed as `engine.build_bid(facts) -> dict`, returning an object that matches the answer
  schema in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md), section "Answer schema".

**Rules for the code.**
- `Decimal` only, never `float`. Components stay unrounded; round half-up once at the end (rule 27).
- No model calls, no network, no browser imports. The engine must run in a unit test in milliseconds.
- Tests use invented numbers only. Nothing read from the websites goes into code or tests.
- Missing facts must not crash: a position whose facts are incomplete is left out, and an optional breakdown field
  that is unknown is omitted (omitted means "unanswered", `0.00` means "a known zero"; they score differently).
- If any position has no matching material, the decision is `no_bid` with no positions and total 0.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Read the bid rules in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md) and the full text with `atira challenge rfq`.
   Write each rule down as one or more cases with invented numbers; these become the tests.
2. `facts.py`, first version, covering the core rules only.
3. Core engine: final quantity (latest clarification, withdrawn clarifications, set-to-piece conversion); price
   condition valid on the scenario date at the highest quantity scale reached; discount (latest approval for the
   exact reference, conditional on a minimum order value); lead time (stock shared between positions of the same
   material, no partial allocation); total; arithmetic consistency.
4. Authority and time as functions over facts: only the latest record not after the scenario date, for the exact
   tender reference, from an authorised sender.
5. Advanced pricing layers, one at a time, each with its tests: which parts the discount applies to, currency
   conversion, metal-index surcharge with validity windows, packaging by carton, shared setup pool, project bonus
   in bands allocated by largest remainders, stroke derived from usable travel.

This stream needs no website, no browser and no test run, so it can start at once. Tell stream C as soon as
`facts.py` covers the core rules; C can then start filling it from the reports.

**Done when** `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes in `agent/` and every rule has at least one
test.

**Not this stream.** Reading websites, prompts, form filling.

## Stream C — lead, submission, runs (Orhun)

**Goal.** The run as a whole: the lead model asks the right questions, the answers become facts, the engine prices
them, and one signed bid is submitted before the clock ends, every time.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/agent.py`, `agent/llm.py`, `agent/models.py`, `agent/run.py`,
`agent/calc.py`, `agent/agent.json`, `agent/pyproject.toml`, `agent/uv.lock`, `agent/tests/test_kit.py`,
`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/` (except the other two push logs).

**Work, in this order.**
1. Baseline: one sandbox test run of the unchanged agent and its score breakdown. It shows where points are lost
   and sets the priorities of streams A and B.
2. Time budget: in a test run the platform's expiry is up to two hours away, and the agent currently plans with
   all of it. Cap the working time at the length of a scored run (20 minutes) minus a margin.
3. Deadline guard: at a fixed margin before the end, submit what is complete and leave unfinished positions out.
   A run without a submitted bid scores 0. After the bid is accepted the process must exit within 10 seconds.
4. Reports to facts: have the lead model put what the sub-agents report into the records of `facts.py`, and call
   the engine instead of the calculator, as soon as stream B delivers the first version.
5. Submission: the form, the signing code from the mailbox, signature, receipt check; validation against the
   schema read at run time.
6. `llm.py`: when a provider's environment variable is missing it falls back to the provider's public address.
   Model calls must only go through the platform's proxy, so remove these fallbacks.
7. Dependencies requested by the other streams (first one: `pypdf` for stream A).
8. Test runs for all streams, every `atira submit`, Entire and the repository.

**Not this stream.** How a page is read (`browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`) and how a price is calculated
(`engine/`).

## Where the streams meet

```
websites ──A──> report (text) ──C──> facts (facts.py, owned by B) ──B──> answer object ──C──> signed bid
```

- **A to C:** the report string from `BrowsingAgent.run()`.
- **C to B:** the records in `facts.py`. B defines them, C fills them.
- **B to C:** `engine.build_bid(facts)` returns the answer object.
- You need a change in a file of another stream: describe it to your human, who asks the owner. Do not edit it,
  not even for a one-line fix; the owner may be changing the same lines.
- You need a new dependency: ask stream C. `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` have one owner so the lock file never
  conflicts.
- Local runs with the scouting logins (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`, with `atira models proxy` running) are free
  and unlimited for everyone. Sandbox test runs are limited to two at a time for the whole team and go through
  stream C; ask for one when you need a score.
- Every push adds an entry to your own push log (`docs/log/<name>.md`, format in AGENTS.md). Read the others'
  new entries after every pull.

## Order of the whole thing (proposal)

1. Now: baseline score (C); core rules as tests and `facts.py` first version (B); per-site report checks (A).
2. Next: core engine wired into the run (B and C); documents and paging reliable (A); second test run.
3. Then: advanced pricing layers (B); submission and deadline guard hardened (C); generalisation check (A).
4. Sunday morning: no new features. The Atira final uses our latest submission that passed review, so the last
   submission before the end must be the most stable one, not the newest experiment. EHL submission is Sunday 12:00.

# Entire — talk notes and setup state (Sat 2026-10-10)

Source: Orhun's two voice recordings of the talk by Entire's CEO (ex-GitHub CEO), ~47 min in total, machine-transcribed
on-device; the raw text stays on his machine (`docs/entire-talk-transcript-raw.txt`, git-ignored). It is noisy;
points marked **(unclear)** need confirmation on Discord. CLI facts below were checked against `entire` 0.11.4 on
Orhun's machine.

## What Entire is

- A CLI that hooks into git and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …). Every time you or the agent commits,
  the agent **session log** (prompts, responses, tool calls) is stored in the same repository as git objects and
  linked to that commit as a **checkpoint**. Checkpoints are pushed with `git push`.
- His framing: code is the most important artifact, the session log is the second. EHL makes Entire mandatory because
  the organizers want to see those session logs.
- Secrets, passwords and tokens are scrubbed from the logs, but his advice is still: never paste API tokens into the
  agent; put them in an environment variable / `.env` and let the agent read it from there.
- The company also runs a distributed git backend (regions in the US, EU/Frankfurt, Australia, India) and a web
  dashboard where sessions can be browsed, filtered to prompts only, and shared by link.

## Setup steps as demonstrated

1. Install the CLI (installer from entire.io). **Done.**
2. `entire enable` in the project folder; it can create the git repo and an initial commit, then asks which agents
   and whether to send anonymous telemetry. **Done** (all eight agents enabled, telemetry on).
3. **Codex: approve the hooks.** Codex has a trust system; on first start in the folder you must trust the folder
   and approve all seven Entire hooks, otherwise Codex sessions are not captured.
   **Not done:** `entire status` currently reports `7 Codex hook(s) need approval · open /hooks`.
4. When a session is captured the agent shows a line like "Entire will link this conversation to your next commit".
5. Create an empty repository on GitHub (he left it public), add it as `origin`, push. **Not done.**
6. Tell the agent once: "commit, and make sure the Entire session is attached". After that it remembers.
   Expected confirmation on push: `[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done` (from the Notion page).
7. On entire.io: log in with GitHub, go through onboarding, pick a region (EU), select the repository. This mirrors
   the GitHub repo to Entire and makes the sessions visible in the dashboard. **Not done.** Whether EHL requires this
   step or only steps 1–6 is **(unclear)**; the Notion page lists only install, enable and the push confirmation.
8. `entire login` in the terminal, which lets the agent search past session logs, including teammates' sessions in
   the same account/repo. He called this the last setup step. **Not done.** Related commands: `entire search`,
   `entire recap`, `entire session list`.

## Advice from the talk that matters for us

- **"Spend an hour tomorrow morning to prepare your pitch."** The jury are humans and weigh the pitch more than the
  product.
- Watch the token budget: do not burn more on API credits than the prize is worth.
- His working model: give agents tasks big enough to run unattended for a long time, with a check at the end, instead
  of many tiny supervised steps. Shared session logs are meant to stop agents repeating each other's mistakes.
- General claims (most code now written by agents, review as the new bottleneck) are opinion, not rules.

## Privacy check — before every commit and before the first push

Entire attaches the full log of every agent session registered in this folder to the next commit, and pushes it.
A session that read anything unrelated to the hackathon must not be attached.

1. `entire session list` — every listed session will be attached. Only sessions started in this folder for
   hackathon work may be there.
2. Remove any other session: `entire clean --session <id> --force`. This clears its state but **not** its data:
   also delete the shadow branch (`git branch -D entire/<base>-<hash>`; it is shared by all sessions on the same
   base commit and is rebuilt on the next turn) and the folder `.entire/metadata/<id>/`.
3. Verify what is left: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <shadow branch> | grep metadata` must list only wanted sessions.
4. A cleaned session registers again on its next turn, so close its window.

State 2026-10-10 ~12:50: one unrelated session was removed this way before anything was committed or pushed.

   - `investigate(site, task)` sends a **browsing sub-agent** (`BrowsingAgent` in `browsing.py`) to one website with
     a task in plain language. The sub-agent drives the browser through a text view of the page (`observe.js`,
     `Tab` in `browser.py`), takes notes, and returns one text report. Several sites run in parallel.
   - `calculate(expression)` does exact decimal arithmetic (`calc.py`).
   - `submit_bid(answer, hints)` checks the answer against the schema, then sends a sub-agent to type the bid into
     the tender website's form, fetch the signing code from the mailbox, sign and confirm.
3. The lead model decides what to ask next from the reports, works out the bid, and submits.

What is weak in this design, and why the streams exist:

- The reports are free text. A value that was read wrongly, or from the wrong record, is not caught anywhere.
- The lead model applies about 28 bid rules by itself, one calculator call at a time. Money is scored to the cent,
  and 75 of 100 points sit in the positions.
- The final run uses different websites. Anything that only works because of how the public websites look fails
  there.

## Stream A — sites and reading (Julien)

**Goal.** A sub-agent that is sent to any of the websites with a task comes back with a report that is complete,
exact (values as shown, with units and dates) and says where each value was read. This must hold on software the
agent has never seen.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/browser.py`, `agent/observe.js`, `agent/browsing.py`,
`agent/browsers.py`, `agent/tests/test_browser*.py`, `docs/log/julien.md`.

**What the other streams rely on (do not change without telling stream C first).**
- `Tab(site_id, page)` and `BrowsingAgent(model, tabs, credentials, task, context, name=..., deadline=...,
  max_steps=..., log=...)`, as `agent.py` calls them today.
- `await BrowsingAgent.run()` returns one string: the report, then the notes taken while browsing.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Run one sub-agent per website on your machine with a survey task and compare its report with what you see in
   the browser yourself. Every difference is a bug in this stream.
2. Documents: PDF and ZIP files, documents inside embedded frames and nested viewers. Known gap: `browser.py`
   imports `pypdf` to read PDFs, but `pypdf` is not in `agent/pyproject.toml`, so in the sandbox every PDF comes
   back as "could not be read". Ask stream C to add the dependency.
3. Lists: paging, "load more", searches that must be narrowed before they show results.
4. Versions: a site that opens an old revision first; the report must say which revision a value comes from and
   which one the site marks as current.
5. Sessions and errors: a session that expires and returns to the sign-in page, error pages that work on a retry,
   popups and dialogs.
6. Look-alike records: the report must name the exact reference, sender and date of what it read, so a record for
   another tender is recognisable as such.
7. Generalisation check: no selector, text, URL or page order that only exists on the public websites. The sign-in
   helper in `browsing.py` finds fields by their type, which is fine; keep it that way.
8. Only when the reports are reliable: fewer steps and tokens per report.

**Done when** a report contains every value the task asked for, as shown on the site, each with its source (page
or document, date, sender, revision), and says plainly what it could not find.

**Not this stream.** Bid rules, arithmetic, the lead model's prompts, the submission flow. Also the pitch and the
development story belong to Julien, outside the code.

## Stream B — bid engine (Uzunov)

**Goal.** One function that turns collected facts into the answer object, correct to the cent, with no model
involved. The same facts always give the same bid.

**Files only this stream edits (all new).** `agent/facts.py`, `agent/engine/`, `agent/tests/test_engine*.py`,
`docs/log/uzunov.md`.

**What the other streams rely on.**
- `facts.py`: typed records (dataclasses) for everything the rules need. Every fact carries where it came from:
  website, document or record, date, sender, revision. This file is the contract between the streams; a change is
  announced in the first line of the commit message.
- One entry point, proposed as `engine.build_bid(facts) -> dict`, returning an object that matches the answer
  schema in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md), section "Answer schema".

**Rules for the code.**
- `Decimal` only, never `float`. Components stay unrounded; round half-up once at the end (rule 27).
- No model calls, no network, no browser imports. The engine must run in a unit test in milliseconds.
- Tests use invented numbers only. Nothing read from the websites goes into code or tests.
- Missing facts must not crash: a position whose facts are incomplete is left out, and an optional breakdown field
  that is unknown is omitted (omitted means "unanswered", `0.00` means "a known zero"; they score differently).
- If any position has no matching material, the decision is `no_bid` with no positions and total 0.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Read the bid rules in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md) and the full text with `atira challenge rfq`.
   Write each rule down as one or more cases with invented numbers; these become the tests.
2. `facts.py`, first version, covering the core rules only.
3. Core engine: final quantity (latest clarification, withdrawn clarifications, set-to-piece conversion); price
   condition valid on the scenario date at the highest quantity scale reached; discount (latest approval for the
   exact reference, conditional on a minimum order value); lead time (stock shared between positions of the same
   material, no partial allocation); total; arithmetic consistency.
4. Authority and time as functions over facts: only the latest record not after the scenario date, for the exact
   tender reference, from an authorised sender.
5. Advanced pricing layers, one at a time, each with its tests: which parts the discount applies to, currency
   conversion, metal-index surcharge with validity windows, packaging by carton, shared setup pool, project bonus
   in bands allocated by largest remainders, stroke derived from usable travel.

This stream needs no website, no browser and no test run, so it can start at once. Tell stream C as soon as
`facts.py` covers the core rules; C can then start filling it from the reports.

**Done when** `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes in `agent/` and every rule has at least one
test.

**Not this stream.** Reading websites, prompts, form filling.

## Stream C — lead, submission, runs (Orhun)

**Goal.** The run as a whole: the lead model asks the right questions, the answers become facts, the engine prices
them, and one signed bid is submitted before the clock ends, every time.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/agent.py`, `agent/llm.py`, `agent/models.py`, `agent/run.py`,
`agent/calc.py`, `agent/agent.json`, `agent/pyproject.toml`, `agent/uv.lock`, `agent/tests/test_kit.py`,
`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/` (except the other two push logs).

**Work, in this order.**
1. Baseline: one sandbox test run of the unchanged agent and its score breakdown. It shows where points are lost
   and sets the priorities of streams A and B.
2. Time budget: in a test run the platform's expiry is up to two hours away, and the agent currently plans with
   all of it. Cap the working time at the length of a scored run (20 minutes) minus a margin.
3. Deadline guard: at a fixed margin before the end, submit what is complete and leave unfinished positions out.
   A run without a submitted bid scores 0. After the bid is accepted the process must exit within 10 seconds.
4. Reports to facts: have the lead model put what the sub-agents report into the records of `facts.py`, and call
   the engine instead of the calculator, as soon as stream B delivers the first version.
5. Submission: the form, the signing code from the mailbox, signature, receipt check; validation against the
   schema read at run time.
6. `llm.py`: when a provider's environment variable is missing it falls back to the provider's public address.
   Model calls must only go through the platform's proxy, so remove these fallbacks.
7. Dependencies requested by the other streams (first one: `pypdf` for stream A).
8. Test runs for all streams, every `atira submit`, Entire and the repository.

**Not this stream.** How a page is read (`browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`) and how a price is calculated
(`engine/`).

## Where the streams meet

```
websites ──A──> report (text) ──C──> facts (facts.py, owned by B) ──B──> answer object ──C──> signed bid
```

- **A to C:** the report string from `BrowsingAgent.run()`.
- **C to B:** the records in `facts.py`. B defines them, C fills them.
- **B to C:** `engine.build_bid(facts)` returns the answer object.
- You need a change in a file of another stream: describe it to your human, who asks the owner. Do not edit it,
  not even for a one-line fix; the owner may be changing the same lines.
- You need a new dependency: ask stream C. `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` have one owner so the lock file never
  conflicts.
- Local runs with the scouting logins (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`, with `atira models proxy` running) are free
  and unlimited for everyone. Sandbox test runs are limited to two at a time for the whole team and go through
  stream C; ask for one when you need a score.
- Every push adds an entry to your own push log (`docs/log/<name>.md`, format in AGENTS.md). Read the others'
  new entries after every pull.

## Order of the whole thing (proposal)

1. Now: baseline score (C); core rules as tests and `facts.py` first version (B); per-site report checks (A).
2. Next: core engine wired into the run (B and C); documents and paging reliable (A); second test run.
3. Then: advanced pricing layers (B); submission and deadline guard hardened (C); generalisation check (A).
4. Sunday morning: no new features. The Atira final uses our latest submission that passed review, so the last
   submission before the end must be the most stable one, not the newest experiment. EHL submission is Sunday 12:00.

# Entire — talk notes and setup state (Sat 2026-10-10)

Source: Orhun's two voice recordings of the talk by Entire's CEO (ex-GitHub CEO), ~47 min in total, machine-transcribed
on-device; the raw text stays on his machine (`docs/entire-talk-transcript-raw.txt`, git-ignored). It is noisy;
points marked **(unclear)** need confirmation on Discord. CLI facts below were checked against `entire` 0.11.4 on
Orhun's machine.

## What Entire is

- A CLI that hooks into git and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …). Every time you or the agent commits,
  the agent **session log** (prompts, responses, tool calls) is stored in the same repository as git objects and
  linked to that commit as a **checkpoint**. Checkpoints are pushed with `git push`.
- His framing: code is the most important artifact, the session log is the second. EHL makes Entire mandatory because
  the organizers want to see those session logs.
- Secrets, passwords and tokens are scrubbed from the logs, but his advice is still: never paste API tokens into the
  agent; put them in an environment variable / `.env` and let the agent read it from there.
- The company also runs a distributed git backend (regions in the US, EU/Frankfurt, Australia, India) and a web
  dashboard where sessions can be browsed, filtered to prompts only, and shared by link.

## Setup steps as demonstrated

1. Install the CLI (installer from entire.io). **Done.**
2. `entire enable` in the project folder; it can create the git repo and an initial commit, then asks which agents
   and whether to send anonymous telemetry. **Done** (all eight agents enabled, telemetry on).
3. **Codex: approve the hooks.** Codex has a trust system; on first start in the folder you must trust the folder
   and approve all seven Entire hooks, otherwise Codex sessions are not captured.
   **Not done:** `entire status` currently reports `7 Codex hook(s) need approval · open /hooks`.
4. When a session is captured the agent shows a line like "Entire will link this conversation to your next commit".
5. Create an empty repository on GitHub (he left it public), add it as `origin`, push. **Not done.**
6. Tell the agent once: "commit, and make sure the Entire session is attached". After that it remembers.
   Expected confirmation on push: `[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done` (from the Notion page).
7. On entire.io: log in with GitHub, go through onboarding, pick a region (EU), select the repository. This mirrors
   the GitHub repo to Entire and makes the sessions visible in the dashboard. **Not done.** Whether EHL requires this
   step or only steps 1–6 is **(unclear)**; the Notion page lists only install, enable and the push confirmation.
8. `entire login` in the terminal, which lets the agent search past session logs, including teammates' sessions in
   the same account/repo. He called this the last setup step. **Not done.** Related commands: `entire search`,
   `entire recap`, `entire session list`.

## Advice from the talk that matters for us

- **"Spend an hour tomorrow morning to prepare your pitch."** The jury are humans and weigh the pitch more than the
  product.
- Watch the token budget: do not burn more on API credits than the prize is worth.
- His working model: give agents tasks big enough to run unattended for a long time, with a check at the end, instead
  of many tiny supervised steps. Shared session logs are meant to stop agents repeating each other's mistakes.
- General claims (most code now written by agents, review as the new bottleneck) are opinion, not rules.

## Privacy check — before every commit and before the first push

Entire attaches the full log of every agent session registered in this folder to the next commit, and pushes it.
A session that read anything unrelated to the hackathon must not be attached.

1. `entire session list` — every listed session will be attached. Only sessions started in this folder for
   hackathon work may be there.
2. Remove any other session: `entire clean --session <id> --force`. This clears its state but **not** its data:
   also delete the shadow branch (`git branch -D entire/<base>-<hash>`; it is shared by all sessions on the same
   base commit and is rebuilt on the next turn) and the folder `.entire/metadata/<id>/`.
3. Verify what is left: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <shadow branch> | grep metadata` must list only wanted sessions.
4. A cleaned session registers again on its next turn, so close its window.

**Goal.** A sub-agent that is sent to any of the websites with a task comes back with a report that is complete,
exact (values as shown, with units and dates) and says where each value was read. This must hold on software the
agent has never seen.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/browser.py`, `agent/observe.js`, `agent/browsing.py`,
`agent/browsers.py`, `agent/tests/test_browser*.py`, `docs/log/julien.md`.

**What the other streams rely on (do not change without telling stream O first).**
- `Tab(site_id, page)` and `BrowsingAgent(model, tabs, credentials, task, context, name=..., deadline=...,
  max_steps=..., log=...)`, as `agent.py` calls them today.
- `await BrowsingAgent.run()` returns one string: the report, then the notes taken while browsing.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Run one sub-agent per website on your machine with a survey task and compare its report with what you see in
   the browser yourself. Every difference is a bug in this stream.
2. Documents: PDF and ZIP files, documents inside embedded frames and nested viewers. `pypdf` is a declared
   dependency since Sat 14:30; before that every PDF came back as "could not be read" in the sandbox.
3. Lists: paging, "load more", searches that must be narrowed before they show results.
4. Versions: a site that opens an old revision first; the report must say which revision a value comes from and
   which one the site marks as current.
5. Sessions and errors: a session that expires and returns to the sign-in page, error pages that work on a retry,
   popups and dialogs.
6. Look-alike records: the report must name the exact reference, sender and date of what it read, so a record for
   another tender is recognisable as such.
7. Generalisation check: no selector, text, URL or page order that only exists on the public websites. The sign-in
   helper in `browsing.py` finds fields by their type, which is fine; keep it that way.
8. Only when the reports are reliable: fewer steps and tokens per report.

**Done when** a report contains every value the task asked for, as shown on the site, each with its source (page
or document, date, sender, revision), and says plainly what it could not find.

**Not this stream.** Bid rules, arithmetic, the lead model's prompts, the submission flow. Also the pitch and the
development story belong to Julien, outside the code.

content.text:
Branch `stream-j` exists, is pushed to GitHub and is checked out. It starts from the latest `main`, which includes Orhun's new branch rules and the `pypdf` dependency. Your uncommitted `.mcp.json` is unaffected.

## Plan for stream J (sites and reading)

The goal from `docs/streams.md`: a sub-agent sent to *any* website returns a report that is complete and exact, gives the source of every value, and says what it couldn't find. I only edit `browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`, `browsers.py`, `tests/test_browser*` and `docs/log/julien.md`. All test runs use Qwen.

**Step 0: measuring setup (first, about 30 min)**
- A local script, kept in the git-ignored `scouting/` folder and never packaged, runs one Qwen sub-agent per site with a survey task and saves its report and step log.
- I compare each report with the scouting notes. Every difference goes on a bug list, which is the stream's item 1.

**Step 1: known bugs from the first local run (high impact, fast)**
- **Stay on your own site:** `goto` refuses URLs outside the sub-agent's own site(s), generically by comparing with the start origin. The first run lost minutes to this.
- **Source on every fact:** `note` automatically stamps the page URL, page title and frame. The model also fills in document, date, sender, revision and status. The report gets a fixed shape: *found* (value, unit, source) and *not found*. `run()` still returns one string, so Orhun's interface stays the same.

**Step 2: sessions and errors (item 5)**
- When a page suddenly shows a login form, the code logs in again and returns to the previous URL by itself.
- Automatic retry on server-error pages.
- A modal dialog in front is listed at the top of the page view with its close button, so the model sees it first.

**Step 3: documents and lists (items 2 and 3)**
- Check reading of PDF, ZIP and documents inside collapsed sections or frames: opening a section waits for its frame to load, plus a tool to open a frame as its own page.
- A `collect_pages` tool: the model picks the "next page" or "load more" control, and the code follows it and joins the results. The rules allow this ("paginate a model-selected result set") and it saves many steps.
- A search showing 0 results is flagged as possibly "too broad, narrow it down".

**Step 4: versions and look-alikes (items 4 and 6)**
- Prompt rules plus report fields: which revision the site marks as current and which one each value came from. The exact reference, sender and date of every record, so look-alikes such as `…-A` or other tenders are recognisable.

**Step 5: generalisation check (item 7)**
- Search my files for anything that only exists on the public sites (texts, URLs, selectors) and remove it.
- Unit tests in `tests/test_browser*.py` on invented HTML pages: hidden decoys, tooltips, collapsed sections, tables, frames, zero-width characters, ZIP and PDF files.

**Step 6, only once reports are reliable: fewer steps and tokens (item 8)**
- Smaller page views and fewer model turns per report.

**Working rhythm:** small commits on `stream-j`, a push-log entry in `docs/log/julien.md` before each push, and a pull request to `main` after each finished step. Sandbox test runs I request through Orhun. Following your token budget, I won't use Claude sub-agents; Qwen does the testing.

One question before I start: should Step 0's script and its saved reports stay in the git-ignored `scouting/` folder, as I'd suggest, or do you want the script committed somewhere?

"""Survey run (stream J): one browsing sub-agent per website, with a generic survey task, against the websites of
`atira scout --env`. It measures how complete and well-sourced the reports are; it is not a unit test.

Skipped unless SURVEY=1, so `python -m unittest discover -s tests` never touches the websites. To run it:

    atira models proxy                          # in another terminal
    eval "$(atira scout --env)"
    SURVEY=1 uv run --no-sync python -m unittest tests.test_browser_survey -v

Options: SURVEY_SITES=erp,mail (default: all), SURVEY_MINUTES=8 (time per site), SURVEY_STEPS=40, HEADLESS=1.
Reports and step logs go to ../scouting/survey/<time>/ (git-ignored: they hold values read from the websites).
"""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

SURVEY_TASK = (
    "Survey this website for everything the brief's task could need from it. Sign in, get past consent pages and "
    "popups, find the records that belong to the tender named in the brief, and open the relevant documents and "
    "records, including other versions so you can tell which one is current. Note every fact the bid rules could "
    "use, each with its source. Also note look-alike records (other references, other senders, other dates) as "
    "such, so they are not confused with the right ones. Read only: do not submit, sign, request codes or change "
    "anything."
)


@unittest.skipUnless(os.environ.get("SURVEY") == "1", "survey run against the websites; set SURVEY=1")
class SurveyRun(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_survey(self):
        stats = asyncio.run(survey())
        for site, row in stats.items():
            self.assertTrue(row["finished"] or row["notes"], f"{site}: no report and no notes")


async def survey() -> dict:
    from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

    from browser import Tab
    from browsing import BrowsingAgent
    from llm import Model

    scouting = json.loads(os.environ["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"])
    access = scouting["access"]
    wanted = [s for s in os.environ.get("SURVEY_SITES", "").split(",") if s]
    if wanted:
        access = [a for a in access if a["siteId"] in wanted]
    credentials = {a["siteId"]: a.get("credentials", {}) for a in scouting["access"]}
    context = f"# The brief (rules apply exactly)\n{scouting['brief']}"
    minutes = float(os.environ.get("SURVEY_MINUTES", "8"))
    steps = int(os.environ.get("SURVEY_STEPS", "40"))
    out = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scouting" / "survey" / time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    model = Model()
    started = time.time()

    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        tabs = {}
        for a in scouting["access"]:  # every site gets a tab, so each knows the others' addresses
            page = await (await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 800})).new_page()
            await page.goto(a["url"], wait_until="domcontentloaded")
            tabs[a["siteId"]] = Tab(a["siteId"], page)

        async def one(site: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
            lines: list[str] = []

            def log(text):
                lines.append(f"[{time.time() - started:6.1f}s] {text}")
                print(lines[-1], flush=True)

            agent = BrowsingAgent(model, {site: tabs[site]}, credentials, SURVEY_TASK, context, name=site,
                                  deadline=time.time() + minutes * 60, max_steps=steps, log=log)
            t0 = time.time()
            report = await agent.run()
            (out / f"{site}.md").write_text(report + "\n\n# Steps\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
            actions = [l for l in lines if re.search(r"\] \w+ \{", l)]
            return site, {
                "seconds": round(time.time() - t0),
                "actions": len(actions),
                "finished": any("finished after" in l for l in lines),
                "notes": len(agent.notes),
                "notes_with_source": sum("source: (not given)" not in n for n in agent.notes),
                "refused_foreign": report.count("Refused:") + sum("Refused:" in l for l in lines),
            }

        results = dict(await asyncio.gather(*(one(a["siteId"]) for a in access)))
        await browser.close()

    summary = json.dumps(results, indent=1)
    (out / "stats.json").write_text(summary)
    print(f"\nSurvey done in {time.time() - started:.0f}s; {model.usage()}\n{summary}\nReports: {out}", flush=True)
    return results


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Stream J unit tests: a sub-agent stays on its own website, and its notes carry their source. Invented hosts only;
no browser, no model, no network."""
import asyncio
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from browser import Tab, origin  # noqa: E402
from browsing import BrowsingAgent  # noqa: E402


class FakePage:
    def __init__(self, url, title="A page"):
        self.url, self._title = url, title
        self.context = self

    def on(self, *args):  # Tab registers its event handlers here
        pass

    async def title(self):
        return self._title


def agent_for(*tabs):
    return BrowsingAgent(None, {t.site_id: t for t in tabs}, {}, "task", "context", name="t", deadline=0)


class OriginTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_origin(self):
        self.assertEqual(origin("https://Shop.Example.test:8443/a/b?c=1"), "https://shop.example.test:8443")
        self.assertEqual(origin("about:blank"), "")
        self.assertEqual(origin("/relative/path"), "")


class ForeignSiteTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        Tab.homes.clear()
        self.portal = Tab("portal", FakePage("https://portal.example.test/login"))
        self.inbox = Tab("inbox", FakePage("https://inbox.example.test/"))

    def test_other_site_of_the_run_is_refused(self):
        agent = agent_for(self.portal)
        refusal = asyncio.run(agent._run_tool("goto", {"url": "https://inbox.example.test/messages/7"}))
        self.assertTrue(refusal.startswith("Refused:"))
        self.assertIn("inbox", refusal)
        self.assertEqual(agent.refusals, 1)

    def test_download_from_other_site_is_refused(self):
        agent = agent_for(self.portal)
        refusal = asyncio.run(agent._run_tool("download", {"url": "https://inbox.example.test/export.zip"}))
        self.assertTrue(refusal.startswith("Refused:"))

    def test_own_site_relative_and_unknown_hosts_pass_the_guard(self):
        agent = agent_for(self.portal)
        self.assertEqual(agent._foreign_site(self.portal, "/tenders?page=2"), "")
        self.assertEqual(agent._foreign_site(self.portal, "https://portal.example.test/docs/1"), "")
        self.assertEqual(agent._foreign_site(self.portal, "https://files.cdn.example.test/spec.pdf"), "")

    def test_an_agent_with_both_sites_may_use_both(self):  # the submission agent works portal and inbox
        agent = agent_for(self.portal, self.inbox)
        self.assertEqual(agent._foreign_site(self.portal, "https://inbox.example.test/"), "")


class NoteSourceTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_note_is_stamped_with_site_page_and_source(self):
        Tab.homes.clear()
        tab = Tab("portal", FakePage("https://portal.example.test/doc/3", title="Spec, revision C"))
        agent = agent_for(tab)
        asyncio.run(agent._run_tool("note", {"facts": "Bore 42 mm", "source": "Spec rev C, 2030-01-02, status valid"}))
        asyncio.run(agent._run_tool("note", {"facts": "Stroke 99 mm"}))
        first, second = agent.notes
        self.assertIn("Bore 42 mm", first)
        self.assertIn("source: Spec rev C, 2030-01-02, status valid", first)
        self.assertIn('read on: portal · page "Spec, revision C" · https://portal.example.test/doc/3', first)
        self.assertIn("source: (not given)", second)
        report = agent._report("FOUND:\n- Bore 42 mm\nNOT FOUND:\n- nothing")
        self.assertIn("NOTES TAKEN WHILE BROWSING", report)
        self.assertIn("read on: portal", report)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

It's skipped unless `SURVEY=1`.

**Step 1: the two known bugs fixed**
- **Stay on your own site:** each `Tab` records its starting origin ([browser.py](agent/browser.py)). `goto` and `download` refuse URLs belonging to another site in the same run and tell the model to list those facts under NOT FOUND. Unknown hosts stay allowed for document servers on the private dataset ([browsing.py](agent/browsing.py)).
- **Source on every fact:** `note` takes a `source` (document, date, sender, revision/status), and the code stamps the site, page title and URL itself. `finish` asks for FOUND (value — source) and NOT FOUND sections.
- **Interface for Orhun:** unchanged.

**Checks so far**
- [tests/test_browser_scope.py](agent/tests/test_browser_scope.py): 6 offline tests with invented hosts, all passing.

content.text:
With checks that would fail if the fixes didn't work. For each fix, here is what I'll look at and where the evidence is weaker.

**Fix 1: assistants stay on their own site**
- **Check:** the step logs must contain no `goto`/`download` to another site's address that went through. Any attempt must show up as `refused_foreign > 0` in the stats, followed by the assistant carrying on with its own site.
- **Weak spot:** the survey task never *asks* for another site, so the assistant may simply not try. A count of 0 refusals then proves little. The first run only wandered because the lead model's task text pushed it there. If the survey shows no attempts, I'd add one targeted live check: give one assistant a task that needs another site ("also check the mailbox for …") and confirm it gets refused and reports the item under NOT FOUND.

**Fix 2: every fact has a source**
- **Check:** in the stats, `notes_with_source` should be close to `notes`. In the saved reports, each FOUND line should have the `value — source: document, date, sender, revision` shape, and each note should have its automatic `read on:` stamp.
- **Correctness:** the format alone doesn't prove the sources are *right*. For the mailbox and the supplier portal, I'll spot-check sources against the scout notes, which list the true sender, date and revision for each mail and spec revision. For example, does the report name the "gültig" revision rather than the first one shown? Is the conditional approval tied to the right sender and date, rather than the decoy for the `…-A` tender?
- **Gap:** for the tender portal and ERP, the scout notes are incomplete, so I can only check those with you looking at the site, or with partial notes.

**What doesn't count as confirmation**
- An assistant that hits its step or time limit and never finishes.
- Reports that look tidy but have values without sources.
- Anything I only judge from the code.

If a check fails, I'll say which one, with the numbers. Fix 2's correctness is also the bridge to the stream's item 1, comparing reports with what's actually on the site, so the gaps I find become the next bug list.

content.text:
## Survey results (Qwen, 4 sites in parallel, 241 s)

| Site | Actions | Finished? | Notes | Notes with source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tender portal | 40 | ❌ hit step limit | 4 | 4 |
| supplier portal | 35 | ✅ | 4 | 4 |
| ERP | 43 | ❌ hit step limit | 1 | 1 |
| mail | 40 | ❌ hit step limit | 6 | 6 |

The run cost 156 Qwen calls and 1.6M input tokens, which is about $0.25 at the simulated price.

**Fix 1, stay on own site: works, but only passively checked.** Every assistant used only its own host, and none tried another, so the guard never fired live (`refused_foreign` = 0 everywhere). The unit tests show the refusal itself works. A live forced check is still open.

**Fix 2, sources: confirmed.** All 15 notes have a source and the automatic page stamp. The sources are also *correct*:
- **Supplier portal:** the report matches the scout notes completely. It picks the *gültig* revision R-6156 as current, lists all 5 requirements with Kataloggruppe, usable-stroke and set notes, and marks the old revisions as superseded.
- **Mail:** each note has the right sender, UTC timestamp and message ID, matching the scout notes.

## New problem found: unfinished reports can mislead
3 of 4 assistants hit the 40-step limit. When that happens, the report says only "(stopped before finishing)" plus the raw notes, with no NOT FOUND list. The mail case shows the risk: its notes contain the **superseded** 5 % approval from 18.01, but not the newer, valid conditional approval from 24.01. The assistant ran out of steps before finding it. The lead model would read "5 %" with a correct-looking source and could use it.

The ERP assistant browsed 43 times and noted only once, so its knowledge was lost when it stopped.

## Proposed next fixes (stream J, small)
1. **Forced wrap-up:** when an assistant hits its step or time limit, one last Qwen call turns its notes into a proper FOUND / NOT FOUND report. That report states what wasn't checked, e.g. "newer approvals not checked".
2. **Note nudge:** after several actions without a note, the assistant is reminded to record what it has read.
3. Then re-run the survey and compare against this baseline.

**Two questions before I commit Steps 0 and 1 to `stream-j`:**
- **Committing:** the team rules say both "commit to your branch as often as you like" (Branches) and "commit only when Orhun asks" (Sessions). Can I commit to `stream-j` now?
- **Entire:** a commit attaches this session's log, which read files outside the repo; the team rules say that must not be attached. Do you want to commit from a fresh session, or clean this session first?

content.text:
Both checks are running, and I'll report when they finish. What I changed in [browsing.py](agent/browsing.py):

1. **Forced wrap-up:** if an assistant runs out of steps or time, one last Qwen call without tools writes the FOUND / NOT FOUND report from its notes. It has to list what wasn't checked, such as newer versions, other folders or further pages. If that call fails, the raw notes come back as before. It stays within the time limit Orhun's lead sets.
2. **Note nudge:** after 6 actions without a note, the assistant is reminded to save what it has read, with its source.
3. **Early warning:** 3 steps before the limit, or 90 s before the deadline, it's told to save its notes and call `finish`. Previously the time warning repeated on every step.
4. **"Look for newer versions" rule:** approvals, revisions and rates can be superseded, so the assistant must check for a newer one before relying on a value. This targets the mail case, where it stopped at the outdated 5 % approval.

**Tests:** 9 offline unit tests pass ([tests/test_browser_scope.py](agent/tests/test_browser_scope.py)), including the wrap-up report, the fallback when the model fails, and both nudges.

## 2026-10-10 16:00 · Survey harness, own-site guard, sourced notes, wrap-up report

- Changed:
  - `tests/test_browser_survey.py` (new): runs one sub-agent per website with a generic survey task against the
    scouting logins and writes stats (time, actions, finished, notes, notes with source, refused requests). It is
    skipped unless `SURVEY=1`; reports go to the git-ignored `scouting/survey/`.
  - `browser.py`: every `Tab` records the origin it started on (`Tab.homes`).
  - `browsing.py`:
    - `goto` and `download` refuse addresses of another website of the same run; unknown hosts stay allowed.
    - `note` takes a `source` (document, date, sender, revision/status) and is stamped with site, page title and
      URL.
    - `finish` asks for a FOUND / NOT FOUND report.
    - A sub-agent that runs out of steps or time writes that report from its notes in one tool-less call, with Qwen
      reasoning switched off, a token cap and at most 90 s. If that call fails too, a report is built in code from
      the notes and the visited pages.
    - Reminders after 6 actions without a note and 3 steps before the limit.
    - Each model call is bounded by the deadline.
    - New prompt rule: look for newer versions before relying on a record.
  - `tests/test_browser_scope.py` (new): 10 offline tests on invented hosts.
- Why: in the first local run sub-agents opened other sites' pages in their own browser, reports had no sources,
  and three of four sub-agents stopped at the step limit with no usable report. One of those had noted only an
  older, superseded record.
- Checked:
  - Unit tests: the 10 new ones pass. The 3 errors in `tests/test_kit.py` are older (the starter test still expects
    `solve()`).
  - Two four-site surveys with Qwen (40 steps per site). Notes with a source: 15/15 and 23/23. Sub-agents that
    finished: 1/4, then 2/4. Notes on the ERP: 1, then 4.
  - The mail sub-agent now finds the governing approval and labels the older one and the look-alikes as such.
  - A forced cross-site task was refused 3 times and the item was reported under NOT FOUND.
  - The wrap-up report was checked live.
- Learned:
  - Qwen reasons before answering. With a token cap the reasoning can use up the whole cap, and the answer then
    comes back empty. Reasoning can be switched off per call (`enable_thinking: False` via `extra_body`).
  - Qwen calls sometimes take minutes, probably when the team's 32 shared slots are full.
  - The shared scouting mailbox collects signing-code mails from everyone's runs.
- For the others:
  - O: `Tab` and `BrowsingAgent` keep the same constructor and `run()` return type.
  - O: reasoning tokens are a large share of time and cost per call; switching reasoning off where it isn't needed
    is worth testing in the lead.
  - O: `tests/test_kit.py` fails on `main`.
  - I: nothing.
- Next: Step 2: re-login when a session expires, retry error pages, show open dialogs first in the page view.
